NOT COVERED — aeon-only rows. Marquee selection, map clipboard (chunk copy/paste), save-as-chunk and the ring-pattern placement tool are AEON features, not classic ones: FACET_TOOLS in src/renderer/workspace/facet-tools.ts gives layout ['stamp-chunk','select','view','marquee','paint-tile','paint-block'] and rings ['place-ring','select','view'], but the s1 manifest declares layout as ['view','stamp-chunk','select'] (src/core/project/s1/index.ts:489) and grants facets ['layout','objects','palette','art'] only — no 'rings', no 'collision'. Their canvas is MapViewport.tsx, which never mounts under a classic open. I verified their absence at runtime (see verified_clean) but did NOT exercise them, because doing so requires opening the aeon project at /home/volence/sonic_hacks/aeon and that working tree currently holds the user's UNCOMMITTED work (3 modified files incl. games/sonic4/data/editor/ojz/act1/section_0.meta.json + 2 untracked paths). __dbg.openDir refuses aeon ('not-classic'), so the only route in is window.api.addRecentProject + a page reload + the recents row, and I judged the risk of an unattributable write into the user's in-flight aeon edits to outweigh the value. Someone should re-run this seat against a throwaway copy of an aeon project — marquee/clipboard/save-as-chunk/place-ring are entirely unverified.

NOT COVERED — save paths. I never pressed Ctrl+S or took the "Save & switch" branch of the dirty-switch dialog, per the LIVE-TREE RULE. So: guarded-write conflict handling, partial-save reporting, dirty-domain clearing after a real save, and the classic-save.ts:'conflict'/'partial' variants are untested here. Related: my finding B1 (no-op stamp dirties) has an unverified downstream leg — I did not confirm what a Save of a no-op-dirty layout actually writes to disk.

NOT COVERED — the "unsaved changes" project-open guard (confirmProjectOpen), sprite-doc and canvas-doc tab interactions with the level loop, tab CLOSE (requestCloseTab, neighbour promotion, stack disposal), Ctrl+1..9 / ⌘K focus routing, and multi-zone viewport records (I only used ghz1/ghz2/mz1).

PARTIAL — collision correctness. I diffed one layout cell (chunk $2D) at zoom 1 pixel-by-pixel against the store's chunkCell data. I did NOT verify colind[block] -> shape selection itself (colind is not reachable from window.__dbg, and I would not import core modules or write into the review tree to get at it), so "the right SHAPE was drawn" is unverified — only "drawn iff solidity != 0" and "every solid cell drew". Path-B collision and the angle ticks' correctness were not checked, only that the toggles are independent.

PARTIAL — object/ring semantics. I verified placement, selection, inspector edit, drag, delete and undo, but not: the player-start drag (startDragRef/classicSetStart) — I ran out of runway; the x/y clamp behaviour at OBJ_X_MAX/OBJ_Y_MAX (GHZ is far too small to reach it); subtype editing and its effect on the drawn sprite; and the fact that ClassicObjectList's only listbox is "Object library" (81 TYPES) — there is no list of the 214 PLACED objects, so entity selection is canvas-hit-test-only. That is documented as deliberate at s1-facets.tsx:271-277, so I did not file it, but a reviewer should decide whether it is still the right call.

ENVIRONMENT CAVEATS THAT COULD HAVE FOOLED ME (and one that did):
(1) The other runtime seat's harness runs `pkill -f '<root>/dist/main/index.mjs'`, which killed MY Electron mid-run three times. Every reported row was re-run to completion on a live instance; nothing is inferred from a truncated run.
(2) Both seats' app instances share one Chromium userData dir, so localStorage carries the other seat's tabs (I repeatedly saw `doc:canvas:cdpa-probe` in my session payload). My FIRST session-restore run (t6-session.mjs) reported "only act 1 restored, act 2 tab lost" — I did NOT report that, because the re-run (t6b) with a full trace showed the restore working perfectly and the earlier result was cross-instance contamination. Finding B2 deliberately rests only on a value my own instance wrote and my own instance read back seconds later, not on the post-relaunch read.
(3) I probed whether concurrent instances clobber each other's session (t15.mjs): they do NOT — a second Aurora process gets a non-persistent localStorage (marker written in instance A read back as null in instance B, and B's write never reached A), because Chromium's LevelDB is locked by the first process. So there is no cross-instance clobber finding; there IS an unfiled, untested observation that Aurora has no requestSingleInstanceLock (src/main/index.ts, 79 lines, no such call), so a second window silently never persists its session — low severity, not chased.
(4) Mid-run the Bash tool's shell died with EDQUOT on the session scratchpad (/tmp/claude-1000 at 3.0G); I moved the whole harness to /var/tmp/cdpb and drove it through the Monitor tool until the shell recovered. Harness sources are at /var/tmp/cdpb/{lib,boot,t1-stamp,t2,t4b,t4c,t5-view,t6b,t7-undo,t8-stamp2,t9,t10,t11,t12,t13,t14,t15}.mjs and are re-runnable with PORT=9366.

findings.title: A layout stamp that writes the byte already there still dirties the act and pushes an undo step
findings.claim: classicSetLayoutCells has no identical-value short-circuit, so stamping a chunk id onto a cell that already holds it commits a real command: the tab gets the unsaved dot, an undo entry is pushed, and the next act switch pops the destructive "Unsaved changes … discards unsaved edits and undo history" dialog for an edit that does not exist.
findings.evidence: Runtime, GHZ act 1 under CDP (harness /var/tmp/cdpb/t9.mjs, section A, real pointer events only). Start state: dirtyTabs=[], Undo chip disabled. Right-click eyedrop on layout cell (3,3) -> selection becomes "Chunk $31" (i.e. the armed id now equals the cell's own id). One left-click with Stamp Chunk on the SAME cell -> re-eyedrop still reads "Chunk $31" (nothing changed) but dirtyTabs=["Green Hill Zone Act 1"] and Undo chip is ENABLED; exactly 1 Undo click drains it back to clean. Code trail: classicSetLayoutCells (classicLevelStore.ts:746-785) validates, builds nextCells, and calls commitLayout unconditionally at :783 — there is no comparison against the existing bytes anywhere on the path; commitLayout (:623) records a history snapshot and applyCommit (:645) merges the dirty patch (:680) without any equality check either. This is an asymmetry, not an oversight of the whole codebase: classicSetStart carries an explicit guard at classicLevelStore.ts:1275-1276 ("No-op guard: an unchanged spawn point records no undo step") and the object-move path guards at ClassicLevelViewport.tsx endObjectDrag (`if (cur.x === drag.preview.x && cur.y === drag.preview.y) { redraw(); return; }`). Consequence chain verified separately in /var/tmp/cdpb/t10.mjs: a dirty act + a click on the sibling act's tab produces alertdialog aria-label "Unsaved changes in Green Hill Zone Act 1" with buttons ["Save & switch","Discard & switch","Cancel"] — so a click that changed nothing can push the user into saving the live disasm back over itself, or into a "Discard" they read as losing work.
findings.fix: Give classicSetLayoutCells the same no-op guard classicSetStart has: after the validation loop, drop any cell whose `grid.cells[y*grid.width+x] === c.chunkId`, and `return { ok: true }` without calling commitLayout when nothing is left. Doing it per-cell (rather than all-or-nothing) also keeps a drag stroke that crosses already-correct cells from recording them.

findings.title: The active level tab's live camera is never snapshotted, so a relaunch reopens it at a stale or default viewport
findings.claim: workspaceStore.setView is only ever called for the OUTGOING act during a tab/act switch, so the tab you are actually looking at when the app exits has its camera persisted as of the last time you switched AWAY from it (or not at all, if you never left it) — the relaunch then restores that stale value, silently discarding every pan/zoom made since.
findings.evidence: Runtime (harness /var/tmp/cdpb/t9.mjs, section B; all tab switches driven by real mousedown on the tab strip). Sequence: open ghz1+ghz2 tabs; focus act 1; setView(1500,200,2); click act-2 tab; click act-1 tab (cam correctly restored to {1500,200,2}); then pan act 1 to {2600,300,4} and STOP there (live readback `__dbg.view()` = {x:2600,y:300,zoom:4}). After the persistence subscription flushed, localStorage['aurora.session.v1:/home/volence/sonic_hacks/s1disasm'] read back from the same live renderer contains workspace {"level:ghz:1":{"facet":"layout","view":{"x":1500,"y":200,"zoom":2}}, "level:ghz:2":{"view":{"x":0,"y":0,"zoom":0.4830729166666667}}} — i.e. act 1 is recorded at the value it had when the user last left it, and act 2 at the default fit that happened to be live when it was left. Code trail: `grep -rn "setView(" src/renderer` shows exactly two writers of useWorkspaceStore.setView, both inside activateLevelTarget — tab-activation/level.ts:86 (classic branch, guarded by `const outgoing = useClassicLevelStore.getState().ref`) and :160 (aeon branch, keyed on `prev.currentZoneId/currentActId`). Nothing snapshots on window close, on blur, or periodically; useSessionLifecycle's persist subscription (session-lifecycle.ts:127-138) serializes whatever workspaceStore already holds, so it faithfully persists the stale record. The RESTORE half is fine and was verified working: in a second, genuinely relaunched process the app came back with the stored tab set and activeId and applied the stored view exactly (post cam == the value in the stored payload). So this is a capture gap, not a restore gap. Separately verified in /var/tmp/cdpb/t6b.mjs: an act that was opened and never left has NO `view` entry at all, and reopens at the fit-to-height default.
findings.fix: Snapshot the ACTIVE tab's live viewStore camera into workspaceStore at the points where it can be lost: (a) a `beforeunload` / `app before-quit` hook in the renderer that calls useWorkspaceStore.setView(activeTabId, {x: vpX, y: vpY, zoom}), and/or (b) have viewStore.setViewport (or the viewport's once-per-frame publish) mirror into the active tab's record — cheap, since the record write only has to happen on a debounce, and it makes tab-activation's outgoing snapshot redundant rather than load-bearing.

findings.title: Collision overlay's surface line is stroked on the cell boundary, so it bleeds one pixel row into the air cell above
findings.claim: drawCollision strokes the per-column surface line at an integer world y with lineWidth 1/scale, so a shape whose surface sits at y=0 of its 16px cell renders half inside that cell and half inside the neighbouring cell above — painting collision ink over chunk cells whose solidity is 0, and rendering the line itself as two half-covered rows instead of one crisp one.
findings.evidence: Runtime pixel diff (harness /var/tmp/cdpb/t4c.mjs): GHZ act 1, layout cell (1,3) = chunk $2D, camera set to zoom 1 so one world px == one device px, cursor parked off-canvas so no hover ghost is drawn. Captured the 256x256 device region for that layout cell with the View menu's "Collision (path A)" OFF, toggled it ON through the real checkbox, captured again, and diffed per 16x16 chunk cell against `__dbg.classic.chunkCell($2D, i)`. Result: 41 cells changed, 32 cells have solidity != 0, 0 solid cells failed to draw (so the two-tier gate itself is honoured), and 9 cells changed despite solidity == 0. Every one of those 9 has exactly n=16 changed pixels confined to local row 15 (the cell's bottom row) and every one has `belowSol: 1` — the cell directly beneath it is solid. Code trail: the body FILL is crisp (`ctx.fillRect(cx + c, cy + ry, 1, run.h)`, classic-overlays.ts:81 — integer rect, no bleed), but the surface pass at :96-118 does `ctx.lineWidth = 1 / ctx.getTransform().a` then `moveTo(cx + c, cy + surfaceY); lineTo(cx + c + 1, cy + surfaceY); stroke()` — a stroke centred ON the integer coordinate, so at surfaceY == 0 it covers device rows -1 and 0 at half coverage each. Toggling the overlay back off restored the region byte-for-byte, so nothing is left behind.
findings.fix: Draw the surface line the same way the body is drawn — `ctx.fillRect(cx + c, cy + surfaceY - (h >= 0 ? 0 : lw), 1, lw)` — or keep the stroke and offset it by half a line width (`cy + surfaceY + lw/2` for a downward-facing edge) so it lands wholly inside the cell it describes.
